---
name: Unknown outreach sends
description: Fail-closed rules for provider responses that do not prove whether an outreach email was accepted.
---

Keep an immutable prospect/campaign-sequence send claim whenever the provider outcome is ambiguous. Transport failures, timeouts, rate limits, conflicts, and server or gateway errors require employee review; they must never release the claim or return the message to an automatically sendable state. Reconcile late provider events using a stable key written before dispatch.

**Why:** An HTTP response can be lost or generated by an intermediary after the provider accepted the message. Releasing the sequence guard on uncertain evidence can create a duplicate email.

**How to apply:** Release a claim only when evidence proves the provider never accepted the request. Provider activity showing bounce, block, or drop is an accepted attempt and must suppress the address, not retry it. Timeouts, missing records, and unknown statuses stay blocked; processed, deferred, and delivered evidence resolves review without redispatch.
